column1: # Deliberate differences between sources/yomitan.json and Yomitan's Spanish rules at d3c54c1 (docs/languages.md 8.2), checked by tools/check-yomitan.mjs.

column7: Yomitan's stem-change rules test X([a-z]*)ending$ but replace the first X of the text (term.replace(/i/, 'e')), even one that a letter outside [a-z] follows; the pack changes the first X that the rule's [a-z]* reaches. Both outputs are not words (británico -> bretánicir in Yomitan, británecir in the pack).
As for present indicative: Yomitan replaces the first i, ie, u or ue of the text, the pack the first one its [a-z]* reaches (sociológicas -> soceológicir, sociológecir).
As for present indicative (pilórica -> pelóricir, pilórecir).
As for present indicative, with the endings -ió and -ieron.
As for present indicative, with the ending -iendo.

For a text that starts with jue, Yomitan's -ar imperative rule changes ue to u and then replaces (a|ue|uen)$, which it does not test: a jue text that ends in e or en without u keeps its ending (juegen -> jugen). The pack has rules only for the endings that give an infinitive.
As for imperative: Yomitan's jue branch replaces (ue|ues|ue|uen)$ after testing (e|es|e|en)$, so juegen gives jugen.

Yomitan's reflexive rule matches the pronoun anywhere in the text and replaces every match (ya me levantar -> ya levantarse); the pack's pattern rules are anchored on the pronoun at the start of the text, where a lookup that starts at the pronoun puts it.
Yomitan's \s+ also takes several spaces, tabs and other white space after the pronoun; the pack's anchor is the pronoun and one space.
